findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition breaks the emoji resize job
findings.body: `downsize` is now defined twice: the 5-argument `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and the 4-argument `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby keeps only the second, so line 145 is dead code. `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with five arguments, which now raises ArgumentError (given 5, expected 3..4). Every custom emoji upload enqueues this job (`app/models/emoji.rb:73`), so emoji are never resized to 100px and the job fails each time. Fix: delete the definition at lines 145-147 and change the call in `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` to `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "100x100", opts)`. A four-argument call `downsize(from, to, w, h)` also now binds `h` to `opts`; no such caller exists in the repository.
findings.originReason: The base had a single 4/5-arity downsize. The diff adds the second definition that overrides it.

verification.reason: Ruby keeps only the second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149), so the 5-argument call `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` in the emoji resize job raises ArgumentError. Every custom emoji upload enqueues that job (emoji.rb:73).

findings.title: Client size limit ignores max_attachment_size_kb and misreports the limit
findings.body: The client limit is now a hard-coded 10 MB for every upload type. Before, it was `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. For attachments, a file above `max_attachment_size_kb` now passes the client check, is uploaded in full, and is then rejected by `Validators::UploadValidator#maximum_attachment_file_size` (`app/models/upload.rb:20`, `lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:37-39` and `84-88`). The alert shows '10240 KB' as the limit, which is wrong for that rejection. Fix: keep the setting lookup for type 'attachment'; use the 10 MB ceiling only for type 'image', since the server now downsizes images.

verification.reason: The client check is now a fixed 10240 KB for every type. Attachments above max_attachment_size_kb (default 3072) pass the client check, are uploaded in full, and are then rejected by the server validator, which uses `max_#{type}_size_kb`.

findings.title: Existing JS test for the too-big check now fails
findings.body: The test `prevents files that are too big from being uploaded` (test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6:52-61) sets `max_image_size_kb = 5`, passes a 10 KB image, and expects `validUpload` to return false with an alert showing `max_size_kb: 5`. With the hard-coded 10 MB limit, the 10 KB image passes and no alert is shown, so the test fails. The pull request does not touch that test file. Either update the test to the new behaviour or restore the setting-based limit for images, as the fix for the attachment finding requires.

verification.reason: The test sets max_image_size_kb=5, uses a 10 KB image, and expects validUpload to fail with an alert showing max_size_kb 5. With the hard-coded 10240 KB limit the image passes, so the test fails.

findings.title: 413 message hard-codes 10 MB instead of the configured limit
findings.body: The 413 branch now always reports 10 MB. The locale text at config/locales/server.en.yml:1037-1038 says the upload limit must match the nginx/proxy `client_max_body_size`, so an operator with a different proxy limit gets a wrong message. Consider deriving the number from the configured limit rather than a constant.

verification.reason: The 413 branch now always reports 10240 KB. The settings text tells operators to configure the proxy client_max_body_size to match max_image_size_kb, so the old setting-based message was the documented value and the constant can be wrong.

findings.title: Downsize failures are ignored and the loop keeps running
findings.body: The loop does not check the result of `OptimizedImage.downsize`. `convert_with` returns false on a non-zero exit or any exception (`app/models/optimized_image.rb:161-168`), so a failed conversion is silent and the loop runs the remaining passes on an unchanged file. The user then receives the validator's generic 'too large' error (`lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:84-86`), which does not say that resizing was attempted. Each pass also runs ImageMagick plus ImageOptim (`app/models/optimized_image.rb:164`), up to five times, and on the synchronous API path (`app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:15-17`) that work runs inside the request. Consider checking the return value and breaking out of the loop when it is false.

verification.reason: The loop ignores the boolean that convert_with returns. When conversion fails, the file stays the same size, so the loop runs all five attempts (each an ImageMagick plus ImageOptim pass) before the validator returns its generic too-large error. On the synchronous API path this all happens inside the request.

findings.title: Animated GIFs over the limit may be flattened to one frame
findings.body: `downsize_instructions` uses `#{from}[0]` (`app/models/optimized_image.rb:129`), so only the first frame is kept. The animated path is chosen only when `from` ends in `.GIF` (`app/models/optimized_image.rb:155`), and the controller passes `tempfile.path` (`app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67`), not the original filename. If Rack 1.5.5 (`Gemfile.lock:231`) creates multipart tempfiles without the original extension, every uploaded GIF over the limit loses its animation silently. Also, when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is off, the GIF is flattened even when the extension matches. Can you confirm that uploaded animated GIFs over the limit keep their animation, and that flattening them when the setting is off is intended?

verification.reason: The non-animated downsize path uses `#{from}[0]`, which keeps only the first frame. The animated path needs both allow_animation and a `.GIF` suffix on the tempfile path, so a GIF is flattened whenever the setting is off and probably also when Rack's tempfile has no extension. I could not check the Rack 1.5.5 tempfile naming because the gem source is not in the repository.

findings.title: API URL downloads no longer bounded by max_image_size_kb
findings.body: The URL download cap is now the constant `10.megabytes` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. The setting no longer bounds API URL fetches, and non-image types can now be fetched up to 10 MB before the validator rejects them (`lib/file_helper.rb:18` only stops once the size check passes). Consider keeping the setting for non-image types, or documenting the new fixed ceiling.

verification.reason: The download cap is now the constant 10.megabytes. Before, it was SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, so non-image URLs can now be downloaded up to about 10 MB before the validator rejects them, and the setting no longer bounds the fetch.

findings.title: SVG is downsized although create_for never resizes SVG
findings.body: The new loop runs on any file for which `FileHelper.is_image?` is true, and that list includes svg (`lib/file_helper.rb:31`). `OptimizedImage.create_for` skips raster resizing for SVG (`app/models/optimized_image.rb:45-47`), which suggests the raster path does not suit SVG. The new loop has no such exemption. Does downsizing an oversized SVG with ImageMagick produce a valid SVG file? Consider excluding SVG as `create_for` does.

verification.reason: FileHelper.images includes svg, and the new loop has no SVG exemption, so an oversized SVG goes through ImageMagick `convert from[0] to`. create_for explicitly skips that raster path for SVG. Whether the output is still a usable SVG is not shown, so this remains a concern rather than a confirmed break.

findings.title: No test covers the new oversized-image path
findings.body: `spec/controllers/uploads_controller_spec.rb` has no case with an image above `max_image_size_kb` (its only size case, lines 85-96, is an attachment). `spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb` only mocks `resize` (lines 33, 42, 76, 85), and nothing covers `downsize`. The failure in the emoji finding would have been caught by any spec of `downsize` or the emoji job. Consider adding a controller spec that uploads an image above the limit and asserts that it is reduced, plus a model spec for `downsize` with the dimensions string.

verification.reason: The only size-related controller spec uses max_attachment_size_kb with a text file, and no spec in spec/ mentions downsize or tests an oversized image going through the new path.

contracts.action: Downsize an oversized image upload in place before Upload.create_for
contracts.before_after: Before: an oversized upload reached Upload.create_for and was rejected by the validator (app/models/upload.rb:20, lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:84-86). After: up to five in-place ImageMagick passes at 80% run while the file is above max_image_size_kb, then the same validator runs. The loop runs inside the request for synchronous API uploads (uploads_controller.rb:15-17) and inside Scheduler::Defer otherwise (uploads_controller.rb:19-22).
contracts.visible_effect: The user either gets the upload accepted at a smaller size or the generic 'too large' error after five passes. The message gives no sign that resizing was attempted.
contracts.failure_mode: convert_with returns false silently on a non-zero exit (app/models/optimized_image.rb:161-168). The loop keeps running on an unchanged file and the user sees the validator error. Nothing is lost, but the work is repeated up to five times. Pre-existing and not changed here: if URL download fails, tempfile is nil (uploads_controller.rb:55 uses rescue nil) and line 72 calls tempfile.size, which raises.

contracts.action: Emoji resize job calls OptimizedImage.downsize with five arguments
contracts.equivalent_path: app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-147 (the five-argument downsize that is now shadowed)
contracts.before_after: Before: the five-argument downsize at optimized_image.rb:145 accepted (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts). After: only the four-argument definition at optimized_image.rb:149 exists, so the same call raises ArgumentError before any conversion.
contracts.visible_effect: Custom emoji are stored at their original size and never reduced to 100px.
contracts.failure_mode: The job raises; no conversion happens and the original emoji file is kept. Emoji are still usable, but the size limit is not enforced.

contracts.action: Client-side size check before uploading a file
contracts.equivalent_path: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:180-186 before this change, which used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']
contracts.before_after: Before: the limit depended on type, so attachments were capped at max_attachment_size_kb and images at max_image_size_kb. After: a fixed 10 MB limit applies to every type.
contracts.visible_effect: Attachments above max_attachment_size_kb pass the client check, upload in full and are rejected by the server. The alert reports 10240 KB, which is not the limit the server enforces.
contracts.failure_mode: Server rejection arrives only after the full upload (lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:37-39, 84-88), and the reported limit is wrong. The error is visible, so nothing is silently lost.

contracts.action: Show the error for an HTTP 413 response
contracts.equivalent_path: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:245-248 before this change, which used Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb
contracts.before_after: Before: the message showed max_image_size_kb. After: it always shows 10240 KB.
contracts.visible_effect: The 413 message states 10 MB whatever the operator configured, which is wrong when the proxy limit is different.
contracts.failure_mode: A wrong number in the alert. The request is still rejected.

contracts.before_after: Before: the cap was SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. After: the cap is 10.megabytes whatever the setting is. The download stops once the size passes the cap (lib/file_helper.rb:18).
contracts.visible_effect: API URL uploads of any type can be fetched up to 10 MB. The validator still rejects non-images above the attachment limit after the download.
contracts.failure_mode: The download uses rescue nil, so a failed fetch yields a nil tempfile (pre-existing, see the first contract).

contracts.action: Animated GIF handling when an oversized GIF is downsized
contracts.equivalent_path: app/models/optimized_image.rb:155 (animated path chosen only when allow_animation is set and from ends in .GIF)
contracts.before_after: Before: no GIF was reprocessed on upload. After: an oversized GIF goes through downsize with allow_animation set to SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails, and the path given is tempfile.path.
contracts.visible_effect: If the animated path is not taken, the upload keeps only its first frame and the animation is lost with no message.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent loss of animation for oversized GIFs. It depends on whether the Rack tempfile path ends in .GIF.
contracts.open_question: Does the Rack 1.5.5 multipart tempfile keep the original .GIF extension? If it does not, animated GIFs over the limit always lose their animation. Also confirm the intent when allow_animated_thumbnails is off.
candidates: the rack 1.5.5 gem's lib/rack/multipart/parser.rb (not in the repository)

contracts.action: Use of OptimizedImage.resize, downsize and optimize after the refactor
contracts.equivalent_path: app/models/optimized_image.rb:49 (the resize call in create_for, which passes width and height)
contracts.before_after: Before: optimize took (width, height) and built the dimensions string itself through the dimensions helper. After: resize and downsize build the string, and optimize takes a dimensions string. The dimensions helper is removed. Only downsize has a second definition, which is the bug above.
contracts.visible_effect: Thumbnail creation via create_for is unchanged. The emoji job breaks (see the emoji contract).
contracts.failure_mode: No other caller of dimensions or optimize exists in the repository (checked with grep).

summary: Read the three files in full and their callers. The clearest defect is in app/models/optimized_image.rb: the new four-argument downsize shadows the five-argument one, so the emoji resize job (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14) now raises ArgumentError on every emoji upload. The client limit in utilities.js is hard-coded to 10 MB for all types; this stops attachment limits from being enforced on the client and breaks an existing JS test that the PR does not update. The controller loop ignores failed conversions and may flatten animated GIFs to one frame; the GIF point is an open question because it depends on the Rack tempfile extension, which I could not check in the repository. No ADRs exist in docs/adr/. I did not build or run anything.
